newsitem.title: USA: Ruiz Massieu got protection money - informant.
newsitem.headline: Ruiz Massieu got protection money - informant.

text.p: A government informant said he twice delivered "protection" money to Mario Ruiz Massieu, a former Mexican official accused of taking bribes from drug-traffickers, according to court documents seen on Tuesday.

The informant also said Ruiz Massieu, who was once deputy attorney general in Mexico, worked for Raul Salinas de Gortari, the ex-president's brother, who either arranged or was present for the money deliveries.
The U.S. government says Ruiz Massieu received the money from drug traffickers seeking protection while he was a Mexican deputy attorney general and top-ranking drug fighter.

The charges were disclosed in an affidavit filed in court last week by Tony Canales, attorney for Ruiz Massieu, in advance of a March 10 civil proceeding in which the U.S. government will try to confiscate a $9 million Houston bank account held by Ruiz Massieu.
Canales filed the affidavit to support a motion seeking permission to take a videotaped deposition of Salinas in his Mexico City jail cell.

Salinas has been held without trial for two years on charges he masterminded the September 1994 assassination of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, brother of Mario and a leader in Mexico's ruling party. Salinas is also accused of illegally compiling a huge fortune while his brother, Carlos Salinas de Gortari, was president.

In the affidavit, Canales said the government informant "testified on two occasions that he allegedly delivered money to Mario Ruiz Massieu for protection. On one of those occasions, the only witness to the transaction, according to the witness, was Raul Salinas de Gortari.
"Further, the other occasion on which the witness allegedly delivered money was allegedly arranged by Raul Salinas de Gortari," Canales said.

"Finally, the witness testified that Mario Ruiz Massieu was a frequent guest at the home of Raul Salinas de Gortari and in fact testified that Mario Ruiz Massieu worked for Raul Salinas de Gortari," Canales said in the document, which was filed with U.S. District Judge Nancy Atlas.

Canales said Ruiz Massieu and Salinas denied the government informant's story and Salinas, through his Mexico City attorney Eduardo Luengo Creel, agreed last week to give a videotaped deposition backing up Ruiz Massieu.
"Creel has advised me that Raul Salinas de Gortari will testify that he never made any kind of payments or arranged for any kind of payments to Mario Ruiz Massieu on anyone's behalf," Canales said.
Creel also said Salinas would say he had had no contact with Ruiz Massieu in the last 20 years and "that Ruiz Massieu did not in any way ever work" for him, Canales said.
It was not yet known if Salinas had been questioned, but Atlas approved the motion to take his deposition.

Last month, the Mexican magazine Proceso quoted sealed court documents as saying Ruiz Massieu received $4 million in a December 1993 meeting with Salinas and a "Marco Torres" at Salinas' ranch in northern Mexico.

Proceso said a government informant charged the payments were part of hundreds of millions paid by drug-traffickers to a group of high-level officials headed by Raul Salinas Lozano, father of the Salinas brothers. The Salinas family has denied the charges.

Ruiz Massieu is out on bond and living in New Jersey, where he was arrested in March 1995 for failing to declare $46,000 in cash he held as he tried to board a flight to Madrid. He left Mexico amid charges that he embezzled money and covered up Salinas' alleged involvement in the murder of his brother.
